set.body:
Deliver actual performance improvement against the pinned comparator, not merely benchmarking infrastructure. Reuse EyeLink workload/evidence tooling and Studio S10.6 responsiveness qualification where suitable.

Acceptance:
- Freeze the required workload matrix, output/scientific equivalence policy, environment, practical effect thresholds, repetitions and aggregation before optimization. Cover ASC/CSV ingestion, pixel-to-degree conversion, filtering/velocity, I-VT/I-DT/microsaccades, QC, AOI/reading, and complete supported pipelines over small, typical and large inputs. Include long stationary I-DT candidates, gaps/noise, high-rate/binocular data and growing data sizes. For eyes4s-only comparisons/studies, use explicit absolute/scaling budgets rather than fictitious pymovements equivalents.
- Measure wall time/throughput, peak process RSS, retained heap, total allocation/GC where available, cold startup separately from warm execution, and p50/p95 interaction latency. Keep platform-specific instrumentation separate rather than equating unlike counters. Identical scientific work/output materialization, tuning opportunities, threads and cache policy must be declared for both implementations.
- Profile and optimize measured bottlenecks without weakening scientific contracts or replacing an equivalent workload with a cheaper one. Start by investigating the historical ASC allocation amplification and I-DT scaling opportunity; neither is a current speed claim.
- Final evidence demonstrates predeclared material aggregate throughput and large-workload memory wins, and no material regression in any mandatory common workflow. Freeze numeric thresholds in the protocol before optimization; unmet thresholds keep this workstream open. Cold-start tradeoffs and CPU/memory Pareto losses remain visible and require an owner decision if they breach the frozen budgets. No cherry-picked single-kernel victory or unweighted average hiding severe regressions.
- Meet existing Studio S10.6 p95 targets on its named machine: selection <100 ms, cached trial switch <250 ms, perspective switch <150 ms, with a documented memory bound. Preserve distinctions between synthetic handler timing and actual display latency.
- Check in reproducible machine-readable baseline/final receipts bound to clean revisions and input hashes. Keep a deterministic scaling/allocation smoke gate and an appropriately scheduled full comparison/regression job. Re-run relevant correctness/conformance gates after optimization.

The first paired baseline slice is intentionally narrow; add separate <=half-day slices for the remaining matrix and each profiled bottleneck. The workstream cannot close after the first workload alone.
set.title: PM3: achieve measured speed, memory and responsiveness gains
